role: import a class-group / idoneal-type finiteness proof (Borwein–Choi for xy+yz+zx) to I3/U(n)
missing_theorem: I3 failure at n (no t,u,v ≥ 3 with (tu−1)(tv−1) = tn+1) forces a class group of discriminant ≍ n to have exponent ≤ 2 (an idoneal-type condition), so Weinberger/Siegel gives finiteness up to one exception. The obstruction is structural. Borwein–Choi's count Σ_z #{divisors of n+z² in (z,(n+z²)/z)} ≍ √n·log n is power-size and a class-number count. The I3 count has the extra condition ≡ −1 (mod t), costing 1/t, so it is ≍ log²n and carries no class-number formula.

role: ES sign as a metacommutation (permutation-sign) invariant of Hurwitz factorisations
missing_theorem: For every p there is a p-tied norm N (e.g. m = (pe+1)/4d from QUATERNION_ES) such that the sign of the Conway–Smith metacommutation permutation on its Hurwitz factorisations is −1 exactly when a certificate exists, and is forced to be −1 for some admissible (d,e). A permutation sign is an order-2 invariant. Order-2 data of p-tied integers is the BM/genus layer, which is pointwise free already. What ES needs is a divisor class, and QUATERNION_ES Prop 2.2 shows the order side is congruence data.

role: genus theory of disc −4N_t: word factorisations N = A·A* as ambiguous classes

The statement is the tied divisor event restated.
